**Anchor Browser** is a cloud-hosted browser automation platform for AI agents. It lets agents use websites much like a person would—navigating pages, filling forms, maintaining authenticated sessions, and extracting information—especially for workflows where there is no usable API.[1]

## How it works

You describe a web task in natural language or integrate through its SDK/MCP tooling. Anchor then runs managed Chromium browser instances, using deterministic automation where possible and AI-driven interaction when needed.[1]

## Typical uses

- Automating internal or third-party web portals without APIs
- Collecting data from web interfaces
- Completing repetitive browser-based operational workflows
- Handling authenticated, cookie-dependent browser sessions
- Exposing browser tasks as callable automation endpoints[2][1]

## Positioning

It is aimed at production-scale browser-agent infrastructure rather than a normal end-user web browser. Compared with conventional browser-automation services, Anchor emphasizes an AI-native “perform web task” abstraction, while still supporting lower-level remote browser control via Chrome DevTools Protocol.[2]
